Definition: Integration of farmer registries, agricultural input vouchers, land registrations, extension services data
Comments: No evidence of agriculture system or farmer registry integration with the UXP or other data exchange platforms. Agriculture digitalization mentioned in broader development plans but not specifically linked to data exchange integration.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original score of 0 (Unknown) understated available evidence. NEC Corporation and Côte d'Ivoire's Ministry of Agriculture launched a digital agriculture project in October 2025 (e-Voucher input-distribution system plus CropScope farm database, initially covering c.30,000 hectares) creating a farmer registry with biometric IDs. This runs under the Ministry of Agriculture and there is no evidence it is connected to the government-wide UXP data exchange platform (launched Sept 2025), whose 12-institution pilot list (per CIO Mag, Oct 2025) does not include the Ministry of Agriculture. Recalculated to 1 (Not integrated): a standalone, evidence-based system exists but is not linked to the national data exchange.
revised_comments: Côte d'Ivoire's Ministry of Agriculture, Rural Development, and Food Production launched a digital agriculture initiative with NEC Corporation in October 2025, comprising an e-Voucher input-distribution system and a CropScope farm database (initial coverage of around 30,000 hectares) that assigns unique biometric IDs to registered farmers. This farmer registry and voucher system operates as a standalone Ministry of Agriculture platform and is not linked to the government-wide UXP data exchange platform, whose initial 12-institution pilot phase does not include agriculture.

Definition: Integration of voter registration data for identity verification, demographic analysis, and service delivery targeting
Comments: No specific evidence of electoral register integration with the UXP platform or other data exchange systems. Electoral Commission operates independently. No documented data exchange integration.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Confirmed absence of integration with more specific evidence. The Commission Électorale Indépendante (CEI) maintains its own biometric electoral register (Liste Électorale Définitive, finalised June 2025 with 8.76m voters) independently, consultable only via the CEI's own website/SMS service. The CEI's own June 2025 press statement notes reliance on paper civil-status documents as a data-quality weakness, indicating no automated link to civil registration or other government data. The UXP interoperability platform's 12-institution pilot (launched Sept 2025) does not include the CEI. Recalculated from 0 (Unknown) to 1 (Not integrated): an evidence-supported negative finding rather than an absence of information.
revised_comments: Côte d'Ivoire's electoral register is maintained independently by the Commission Électorale Indépendante (CEI) through its own biometric voter database, with the definitive electoral list (8.76 million voters) finalised in June 2025 and accessible only via the CEI's own website and SMS service. The CEI has itself noted that it still relies on paper-based civil-status records rather than an automated feed, and the government's new UXP interoperability platform's initial pilot phase (launched September 2025, 12 institutions) does not include the electoral commission. There is no integration between the electoral register and the government data exchange.

Definition: Integration of job seeker registries, unemployment insurance, public employment programs, labor market information
Comments: No specific evidence of employment services or labor market data integration with the UXP or other government data exchange platforms in Côte d'Ivoire.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Substantial new evidence found that was absent from the original 0/Unknown score. The Observatoire National de l'Emploi et de la Formation (ONEF) officially launched the Système d'Information sur le Marché du Travail (SIMT) on 23 June 2026, built on the SDMX data-exchange standard and integrating labour-market data from CNPS (social security), CGRAE (state pension fund), Agence Emploi Jeunes and the national statistics agency, among others. At launch, 91 of 134 planned indicators were live across 299 statistical tables/dashboards. This is a genuine, operational, multi-institution data-exchange integration for employment/labour-market data, financed via World Bank PEJEDEC III with ILO technical support. Recalculated from 0 (Unknown) to 4 (Partially integrated): the system is functional and cross-institutional but continued data population is still described by officials as the primary ongoing task, so it is not yet 'fully' integrated.
revised_comments: Côte d'Ivoire's Observatoire National de l'Emploi et de la Formation (ONEF) launched the Système d'Information sur le Marché du Travail (SIMT) on 23 June 2026, a labour-market data-exchange platform built to the international SDMX (Statistical Data and Metadata eXchange) standard. It integrates employment and labour data from multiple bodies, including the Caisse Nationale de Prévoyance Sociale (CNPS), the Caisse Générale de Retraite des Agents de l'État (CGRAE), the Agence Emploi Jeunes and the national statistics agency. At launch, 91 of a planned 134 indicators were already accessible across 299 statistical dashboards, with financing from the World Bank (PEJEDEC III) and technical support from the ILO. Data integration and population of the platform are ongoing and expected to expand further.

Definition: Integration of driver's license registration and traffic offence data
Comments: No evidence of driver licensing or traffic system integration with the UXP or other data exchange platforms in Côte d'Ivoire.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: New evidence found that the original 0/Unknown score missed. Since a July 2025 Ministry of Transport communiqué, traffic police can verify driving licence validity in real time against an online government database during roadside checks, and a points-recovery register is centralised at OSER. A 2021 decree already authorised Quipux Afrique/Ministry of Transport to run an interconnectable 'Système de Transport Intelligent' covering driving licences, vehicle registration and traffic offences. By May 2026, the CGI Digital mobile app allows citizens to view their digital driving licence and real-time points balance. This constitutes operational, cross-agency (police/transport ministry/citizen) data use, though there is no evidence it is yet linked into the broader UXP whole-of-government exchange. Recalculated from 0 (Unknown) to 4 (Partially integrated).
revised_comments: Côte d'Ivoire's Ministry of Transport, through its partnership with Quipux Afrique (under a 2021 decree establishing an interconnectable 'Système de Transport Intelligent'), operates a digital database of driving licences and traffic offences. Since July 2025, traffic police have been able to verify licence validity in real time against this online database during roadside checks, and a licence points-recovery service is centralised at the Office de Sécurité Routière (OSER). Since May 2026, the CGI Digital mobile application (available on the App Store and Google Play) has allowed drivers to view their digital licence and real-time points balance directly on their phones. Integration currently spans the transport ministry, traffic police and citizens, though it is not confirmed to be linked to the broader government-wide UXP interoperability platform.

Definition: Is artificial intelligence integrated into the data exchange for data quality, fraud detection or predictive analytics
Comments: No evidence of AI integration in the new UXP-based data exchange platform. The National Cybersecurity Strategy (2026-2030) is being developed. Absence of specific laws governing AI development noted by Trade.gov. No documented AI use cases in government data exchange.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original 0/Unknown score is refined with fresh evidence rather than simply confirmed. Côte d'Ivoire adopted a National AI Strategy in 2025 (to 2030) that explicitly describes AI adoption within public administration as 'embryonic' and treats AI-enabled fraud detection/data-quality tooling as a future goal, not a current capability. The one concrete AI deployment identified in government service delivery is the EMY 101 WhatsApp/Messenger chatbot (launched March 2026), a citizen-information assistant, not a data-exchange fraud-detection/analytics tool. No official description of the UXP data exchange platform (launched Sept 2025) mentions AI, data-quality or fraud-detection functionality. Recalculated from 0 (Unknown) to 1 (No): there is now positive evidence of absence rather than simply no information.
revised_comments: Côte d'Ivoire adopted a National Artificial Intelligence Strategy in 2025 (running to 2030), which explicitly characterises AI adoption within public administration as embryonic and treats AI-enabled fraud detection and data-quality tooling as future ambitions rather than existing capability. The one operational AI tool in government service delivery to date is 'EMY 101', a WhatsApp/Messenger chatbot launched in March 2026 that answers citizens' administrative queries; it is a citizen-facing information assistant rather than an analytics or fraud-detection function embedded in the UXP data exchange. No AI, data-quality or predictive-analytics capability has been documented within the UXP interoperability platform itself.

Definition: Level of public transparency regarding data exchange operations, governance, and data sharing agreements
Comments: Ministry of Digital Transition leads with public announcements. ARTCI publishes annual reports. SNDI announces platform launch publicly. Limited public dashboard for data exchange operations. The Cybernetica UXP launch ceremony was publicly announced with media. No real-time public transparency dashboard documented.
redteam_note: Value Name differs from the scale label — usually cosmetic.
revision_notes: Confirmed. Original sources (wearetech.africa, dataprotection.africa) were verified and remain accurate, though the dataprotection.africa page (last updated May 2022) is dated and adds little on the data exchange itself. Fresher, more relevant sources found: the Ministry's own official announcement (telecom.gouv.ci) and CIO Mag's detailed October 2025 report, which discloses the project cost (500m FCFA/€387,350), the 12 pilot institutions, and a 2027 full-rollout target. ARTCI (the ICT/telecoms and data-protection regulator, one of the supervising bodies) is statutorily required to publish an annual activity report, though this covers the wider ICT/telecoms sector rather than the UXP exchange specifically. No dedicated public dashboard or standalone governance/data-sharing-agreement disclosure for the exchange itself was found. Score of 2 (Low – Limited Disclosure) remains the best fit: disclosure is via one-off launch publicity and general regulator reporting, not routine, exchange-specific public reporting.
revised_comments: Public information on Côte d'Ivoire's UXP government data exchange platform is disclosed through official ministerial and press announcements rather than routine, dedicated reporting. The Ministry of Digital Transition and Digitalisation (via SNDI) publicly launched the platform on 25 September 2025 in Abidjan, with subsequent press coverage disclosing details such as the €387,350 (approximately 254 million FCFA) initial contract value, the 12 pilot institutions, and a target of full rollout by 2027. The telecommunications/ICT and data-protection regulator ARTCI is required to publish an annual activity report covering the wider ICT sector, but no dedicated public dashboard or standalone transparency report specific to the data exchange's governance or data-sharing agreements has been identified.
